study.title: Let everything that has breath praise the LORD
study.intro: Psalm 150 is the grand finale of the whole book of Psalms. Every one of its six verses calls for praise: where to praise God (His sanctuary and the heavens), why to praise Him (His mighty acts and excellent greatness), how to praise Him (with every instrument and with dancing), and who should praise Him (everything that has breath). After 149 psalms of joy, grief, confession and hope, the book ends in pure praise.
study.context: Psalm 150 serves as the doxology for Book V and for the whole Psalter, just as Psalms 41, 72, 89 and 106 close the earlier books with praise. Thirteen times it says 'praise' (hallelu). Its instruments span temple worship: the priests' ram's horn, the Levites' harps and lyres, women's tambourines, and cymbals. The final verse opens worship to every living, breathing creature.
study.peopleNote: No author or individual is named. Everything that has breath is called to praise. God is never portrayed as a human figure in planned art.

verses.title: Where to praise
verses.heading: Praise God in His sanctuary
verses.meaning: 'Hallelujah! Praise God in His sanctuary. Praise Him in His mighty heavens.' The final psalm answers the question 'where?' Praise God in His sanctuary, the temple on earth, and in the mighty heavens above. Praise fills every place, from the gathered worship of God's people to the vast skies. There is nowhere praise does not belong.
verses.context: The sanctuary was the temple in Jerusalem, God's dwelling among His people. Psalm 29:9 says in His temple all cry, 'Glory!' Revelation 5:11-13 shows praise filling heaven and earth together.
explore: Sanctuary
The holy place, God's temple where His people gathered to worship Him.
Mighty heavens
The great expanse of the sky, displaying God's power and glory.
verses.reflect: Where can you praise God this week, both with others and alone under the sky?
verses.alt: A temple courtyard open to a vast sky full of light.

verses.title: Why to praise
verses.heading: Praise Him for His excellent greatness
verses.meaning: 'Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him for His excellent greatness.' Now the reason: God's mighty acts and His surpassing greatness. We praise Him for what He does, creating, rescuing, providing, and for who He is, great beyond all measure. The whole book of Psalms has told His mighty acts; now it simply calls us to respond.
verses.context: Psalm 145:4 says one generation will proclaim His mighty acts to the next. Deuteronomy 3:24 asks what god in heaven or earth can do deeds like Yours. Psalm 145:3 says His greatness is unsearchable.
explore: Mighty acts
God's powerful works in creation, history and salvation.
Excellent greatness
God's surpassing majesty, beyond all comparison and measurement.
verses.reflect: Name one mighty act of God and one quality of His greatness you can praise Him for today.
verses.alt: A wide valley with river, fields and mountains under a bright sky.

verses.title: Horn, harp and lyre
verses.heading: Praise Him with the sound of the horn
verses.meaning: 'Praise Him with the sound of the horn; praise Him with the harp and lyre.' Now the 'how': with music. The horn, a ram's horn called the shofar, was blown by priests to call people to worship and announce festivals. Harps and lyres were played by Levites. Every instrument can be dedicated to God's praise, loud trumpet blasts and gentle strings alike.
verses.context: Leviticus 25:9 commands blowing the horn on the Day of Atonement. 1 Chronicles 15:16 describes Levites appointed to play harps, lyres and cymbals. Joshua 6:20 tells of horns blown at Jericho.
explore: Horn
The shofar, a ram's horn trumpet blown by priests to call people to worship.
Lyre
A stringed instrument held in the hands and plucked, used by David and the Levites.
verses.reflect: What gift or skill, musical or not, could you offer to God as praise?
verses.alt: A ram's horn, a harp and a lyre resting together on temple steps.

verses.title: Tambourine and dancing
verses.heading: Praise Him with tambourine and dancing
verses.meaning: 'Praise Him with tambourine and dancing; praise Him with strings and flute.' The music gets more joyful. Tambourines and dancing were part of celebrations, like Miriam's song at the Red Sea. Strings and flutes add melody. Praise can be festive and full of movement. God welcomes the whole range of joyful expression.
verses.context: Exodus 15:20 tells of Miriam leading women with tambourines and dancing. Psalm 149:3 says praise His name with dancing. Jeremiah 31:13 promises young women will rejoice in the dance.
explore: Strings
Stringed instruments of various kinds, plucked or played to make melody.
Flute
A wind instrument made of reed or bone, played at celebrations and festivals.
verses.reflect: How might you bring more joyful celebration into your worship?
verses.alt: Villagers dancing in a circle with tambourines and flutes at a festival.

verses.title: Clashing cymbals
verses.heading: Praise Him with resounding cymbals
verses.meaning: 'Praise Him with clashing cymbals; praise Him with resounding cymbals.' The music builds to a crescendo with the loudest instruments, cymbals crashing and ringing. Praise is not only quiet reflection; sometimes it is loud and exuberant. The psalm imagines a sound so full that it fills every corner. God deserves our loudest joy.
verses.context: 1 Chronicles 16:5 names Asaph sounding cymbals before the ark. 2 Chronicles 5:12-13 describes the temple dedication with cymbals and trumpets when God's glory filled the house. Ezra 3:10 tells of cymbals at the rebuilding of the temple.
explore: Cymbals
Pairs of metal plates struck together to make a loud ringing crash.
Resounding
Loud and echoing, filling a space with ringing sound.
verses.reflect: When was the last time you praised God with loud, exuberant joy?
verses.alt: Musicians striking bronze cymbals on temple steps with sunlight flashing.

verses.title: Everything that has breath
verses.heading: Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!
verses.meaning: 'Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Hallelujah!' The book of Psalms ends with an invitation to every living creature. If you have breath, you have a reason and a calling to praise God. Breath itself is His gift. After all the laments, confessions and prayers of the Psalms, the final word is praise. This is where God's story is headed, and where every life finds its purpose.
verses.context: Genesis 2:7 says God breathed into man the breath of life. Revelation 5:13 pictures every creature in heaven and on earth praising God. Psalm 145:21 says let every creature bless His holy name forever.
explore: Breath
The air of life that God gives to every living creature.
Hallelujah
'Praise the LORD,' the closing word of the whole book of Psalms.
verses.reflect: As you breathe right now, how can you turn that breath into praise?
verses.alt: People and animals across a sunlit landscape with birds rising into the sky.
